description:
Return the citation-anchored specification for one Eurorack module by id.

Use this when the user names a specific module and you want its specs: HP, depth, power, jacks (inputs/outputs with voltage ranges and signal types), parameters (controls with ranges and units), modes, hidden functions and firmware history.

Every typed row carries a source_id pointing at the manufacturer document it came from; list_references(module_id=...) gives each source's title and canonical_url.

Module IDs are slug-shaped: "<manufacturer-id>/<module-slug>", e.g. "make-noise/maths", "alm-busy-circuits/pamelas-new-workout".

## Optional args — trim the payload
  - view: "concise" returns the id-card fields (name, manufacturer, hp, description, production_status). "full" (default) returns everything. Ignored when fields is set.
  - fields: array of top-level keys to include (e.g. ["jacks","parameters"]). id and _meta are always returned. Takes precedence over view.

Returns:
  - id, name, manufacturer { id, name }, hp, depth_mm, power { plus_12, minus_12, plus_5 } (mA)
  - description: short summary of the module (a typed record replaces this field in a later release)
  - jacks[]: { id, name, direction, signal_type, voltage_min, voltage_max, description, source_id, assignments[], normalled_from, tracking?, _field_absent? }. normalled_from { id, name } names the jack an unpatched input receives. _field_absent.<field> means the manual was checked and doesn't state that field; a null field WITHOUT an entry means it hasn't been extracted yet.
  - parameters[]: { id, name, control_type, range_min, range_max, range_unit, default_value, behavior, min_firmware, source_id, zones[], assignments[], per_mode_notes?, _field_absent? }
  - modes[]: { id, label, description, source_id, scope? } for modal modules; empty otherwise
  - hidden_functions[]: { id, trigger_type, affected_control, label, description, source_id } — functions reached by long-press, hold, combo, etc.
  - panel_sections[]: manufacturer-named panel regions with members cross-referencing jacks[] / parameters[] by id
  - firmware_versions[]: { version, release_date, notes, source_id }
  - record: the typed record, or null when the module hasn't been extracted yet. Layers: blocks[] (named circuits with their controls/inputs/outputs), jacks[] (direction, signal_types, function, voltages, polarity, scaling, threshold_v, pulse_ms, coupling, audio_rate, normalled_from, attenuated_by, feeds / sourced_from / selected_by, per_mode, types, not_stated), controls[] (function, range, positions, affects, per_mode), modes[], hidden_functions[], specs[] (quantity, min/max/value, unit, condition), properties[] (subject/property/value), rules[] (subject / when / effect, optional mode), tags[] (function tags with evidence). Every element cites src, a source_id. Labels are the manual's own terms, never quotes. A field listed in a jack's not_stated was checked and the manufacturer doesn't state it; a null field not listed there is unknown. Where the record and the older jack/parameter fields disagree, prefer the record.
  - reference_url: the manufacturer's canonical manual URL
  - audit_url, production_status ("current" | "discontinued")
  - _meta: source_count, last_verified

Errors:
  - "Module not found: <id>" if no module with that id exists.

If the manufacturer's documents don't cover the question, say so — never infer from spec data.

fields.description: Optional: top-level keys to include (e.g. ["jacks","parameters"]) when you only need a slice and want to skip the full payload. Omit for everything. id and _meta are always returned. Takes precedence over `view`. Selectable: manufacturer, name, hp, depth_mm, power, description, jacks, parameters, modes, hidden_functions, _field_absent, panel_sections, firmware_versions, reference_url, audit_url, production_status, record.

view.description: Optional: "concise" returns the id-card subset (name, manufacturer, hp, description, production_status) and drops the heavy arrays. "full" (default) returns the complete spec. Ignored when `fields` is set.

name: get_module
title: Look up module
